newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts says tobacco settlement not imminent.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts says tobacco settlement not imminent.

text.p: Massachusetts is in talks with at least two tobacco companies about a possible settlement of suits to recover the costs of treating smokers, but a settlement is not imminent, a spokesman for the state attorney general said on Wednesday.

"The office is involved in discussions with those two companies, at least, on a settlement," said the spokesman. He was referring to Philip Morris Cos Inc, the maker of Marlboro, and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.
But the spokesman for the Massachusetts Attorney General, Scott Harshbarger, appeared to rule out finding a quick solution, saying: "A settlement is not imminent."
No further information on the Massachusetts negotiations with tobacco companies was immediately available.

Minnesota Attorney General Hubert Humphrey earlier said that executives for the largest cigarette companies have been meeeting for the first time with state attorney generals to discuss a possible settlement.

He told Reuters that while this was a major step, he was not satisfied with the proposals he had heard so far. Humphrey is one of 22 attorney generals who have sued the tobacco industry to recoup the expenses states have incurred to treat smokers.
